assessment.nobel_worthiness: Chemically induced proximity that hijacks E3 ligases to destroy a target protein is a new drug modality built on molecular design: bifunctional molecules and molecular glues give precise control over recognition. It changes what chemists and clinicians can do, since proteins once called undruggable can now be removed, and it has spread through chemical biology and medicine.
assessment.attribution: Crews and Deshaies founded the PROTAC concept and the first proof-of-principle work. Ciulli contributed VHL ligands, ternary-complex structure and design rules. The molecular-glue branch (Handa, Ito, Gray) is a distinct lineage and a credit-allocation problem; I would keep the prize centred on the rational bifunctional degrader concept.
assessment.maturity: Many independent groups reproduce the concept and several degraders are in late-stage clinical trials. Timing looks right, though clinical approval is still to come.
uncertainties: Whether the prize should cover PROTACs only or also molecular glues and the cereblon mechanism of thalidomide analogs.
Clinical benefit is not yet established by an approved PROTAC drug, as far as I know; I have not verified current trial status.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Ionizable lipid nanoparticles are the molecular delivery technology that turned nucleic-acid medicines, including the mRNA vaccines, into real products. Control of lipid pKa, self-assembly and endosomal escape is a chemistry design achievement with huge societal reach.
assessment.attribution: Credit is spread across Cullis and colleagues (early lipid-nanoparticle formulation and ionizable-lipid work), Anderson and Langer (combinatorial lipid libraries) and industry inventors. A fair trio is hard to draw and the decisive contributions are contested.
assessment.maturity: Validated at a very large scale by the clinical and public-health record, so recognition is timely. The 2023 Medicine prize covered the mRNA modification science, not the delivery chemistry.
uncertainties: Allocation among Cullis, Hope, Anderson, Langer, MacLachlan and Madden is unresolved, and patent disputes may affect perceptions.
Whether the committee sees this as pharmaceutical formulation rather than a fundamental chemical discovery.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Base editing converts one base into another without double-strand breaks, using engineered deaminase fusions. It is protein and chemical design applied to the genome and gives precise control over a molecular outcome, with a direct route to patient therapies.
assessment.attribution: Liu is the clear intellectual driver, with Komor and Gaudelli as lead trainees on the cytosine and adenine editors. The Nishida and Kondo work is related but earlier or parallel. A single-laureate prize for Liu is the cleanest configuration, though a shared prize with Nishida or Kondo could be argued.
assessment.maturity: Widely replicated, with clinical trials under way and early patient results, but long-term safety and efficacy data are still limited. Possibly slightly early; the CRISPR prize of 2020 sets a precedent for genome editing.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2020 CRISPR prize and with prime editing (B015) may lead the committee to treat Liu's work as one package.
Clinical track record is still short.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Genetic code expansion lets cells incorporate noncanonical amino acids at chosen sites through orthogonal tRNA/synthetase pairs. This gives chemists direct control over protein composition and enables new probes, crosslinkers, biosensors and therapeutic proteins. It has had broad impact in chemical biology.
assessment.attribution: Schultz founded the field with the first orthogonal pairs in bacteria and yeast. Chin extended it to multicellular organisms and to quadruplet and orthogonal ribosome systems. Wang made early contributions in mammalian cells and with Schultz on the first in vivo work. Mehl and Yokoyama are also credited and the allocation could be debated.
assessment.maturity: Mature, with decades of independent use and broad adoption, so the work is not premature. Waiting has created some queue pressure from adjacent chemical biology topics.
uncertainties: Relative contribution of Chin and Wang compared with Schultz is open to debate.
Overlap with Suga's Flexizyme work and with the chemical protein synthesis candidates.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Massively parallel sequencing, built on reversible-terminator chemistry, clonal amplification and pyrosequencing, made genome-scale readout cheap and routine. It is a major transformation for biomedicine, grounded in chemical and analytical innovation.
assessment.attribution: Balasubramanian and Klenerman developed Solexa sequencing-by-synthesis chemistry. Rothberg led the 454 pyrosequencing platform. Mayer and Ju are other credited contributors. The sequencing field has overlapping and competing claims between platform companies.
assessment.maturity: Thoroughly proven over almost twenty years and a standard research and clinical tool, so recognition would be timely or overdue.
uncertainties: The Sanger and Gilbert sequencing prize of 1980 may lead some to judge this a technical advance, not a new chemistry concept.
Commercial claims and patent history make attribution contested.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Single-molecule readout of nucleic acids through nanopores is a clear case of a physical-chemical sensing idea becoming a field-deployable analytical tool. It links directly to my own interest in biosensing, and enables long-read sequencing and single-molecule analysis.
assessment.attribution: Branton, Deamer, Kasianowicz and Church contributed the early concept, while Bayley engineered protein pores and Akeson showed enzyme-controlled DNA translocation. I believe Branton has died, which would exclude him, but I have not verified this. The decisive credit is spread out.
assessment.maturity: Established, with a commercial instrument in wide use, but accuracy and the range of applications are still developing.
uncertainties: Branton's status and how to allocate credit among the pioneers.
Whether the committee sees the work as physics or biophysics rather than chemistry.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Phase separation as an organizing principle gave cell biology a physical-chemical language for membraneless organelles. It ties to my interest in self-assembly of peptides and proteins, and has opened new thinking on disease and drug action.
assessment.attribution: Hyman and Brangwynne showed liquid-like P granules and nucleoli. Rosen provided the multivalent-interaction model with synthetic systems. Pappu and Mittag contributed physical-chemistry theory and sequence grammar. The set of laureates is not obvious.
assessment.maturity: Influential but still evolving; the physiological relevance of condensates is debated and many claims lack rigorous in-cell confirmation.
uncertainties: Controversy over whether in-cell structures are truly phase-separated.
Possibly more cell biology or physics than chemistry and the discovery may be better placed with another Nobel committee.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: DNA origami and tile assembly show programmable bottom-up design of nanoscale structures, with applications in biosensing, nanophotonics and molecular machines. It is a clear example of design principles giving precision over assembly.
assessment.attribution: Rothemund introduced scaffolded origami and Winfree developed algorithmic assembly and kinetic design. Yin built single-stranded tile and strand-displacement systems. Seeman, the originator of structural DNA nanotechnology, is not on the supplied list, which complicates a fair prize.
assessment.maturity: Well confirmed and widely used, though practical impact beyond research tools is still limited.
uncertainties: The absence of the field's founder from the credited names.
